steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Job production: one-off, unique products made to customer specification (e.g. custom wedding cake). High quality, high price, but slow and labour-intensive.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Batch production: groups of identical products made together (e.g. bakery making 50 loaves). Allows some variety but requires cleaning/resetting between batches.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Flow (mass) production: continuous, standardised production on an assembly line (e.g. car manufacturing). High volume, low unit cost, but high set-up costs and inflexible.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Productivity measures output per unit of input: labour productivity = output / number of workers. Higher productivity means lower unit costs and greater competitiveness.

steps.body: Job production advantages: unique, high-quality products that command premium prices; fully customised to customer needs. steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: When comparing production methods, always link back to the specific business context - there is no universally 'best' method. Productivity questions: always show the formula and explain what affects the ratio (training, technology, motivation). Lean production is about eliminating waste - always define what waste means in the specific context.
